A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same eSEN research work. All 19 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-D, support comparison without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-dynamics simulations, architecture ablations, materials and molecular benchmark evaluations, phonon analyses and inference-speed measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for eSEN trained on OMat24 and subsequently fine-tuned on sAlex/MPTrj.

M1.justification: Sections 4-5 retain the eSEN architecture, conservative-force inference and direct-force pretraining followed by conservative fine-tuning. The OMat/OAM variants reuse existing method components with different training data and configurations; no new algorithmic component or loss formulation is introduced.

E1.justification: v2 substantially expands inorganic-material training coverage beyond MPTrj by training on OMat24 and fine-tuning on sAlex combined with MPTrj. sAlex was already present in v1 as a 5,000-sample evaluation set, but its use for training is new. The existing molecular datasets, MD scenarios and evaluation benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds MatRIS-MP, AlphaNet-MP and DPA3-v2-MP, and removes SevenNet-0 from that comparison while retaining it in the phonon comparison. New non-compliant comparisons in Tables 3-4 introduce numerous additional baselines, including eqV2-M-OAM, ORB v3, SevenNet-MF-ompa, GRACE-2L-OAM and MatterSim. The corresponding MPTrj Orb and GRACE entries are matched across their naming changes.

E3.justification: Existing splits and MD/phonon evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Added OMat/OAM runs use two direct-force and two conservative training epochs, followed by one fine-tuning epoch on sAlex plus eight copies of MPTrj; they use 64 radial basis functions and omit DeNS during OMat training. Table 2 adds structural RMSD reporting and drops recall. These extend the settings without redesigning the existing evaluations.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends the 0.01-versus-0.2 Å displacement comparison to eqV2-M-OAM. Section 6.2 also reports OMat-only phonon errors before sAlex/MPTrj fine-tuning, providing a limited additional comparison of training stages. The original architecture ablations, correlation analyses, displacement sweeps, phonon case studies and efficiency analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The point-estimate benchmark reporting and averaging over 81 TM23 and seven MD22 systems remain unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial non-compliant benchmark results: eSEN-30M-OAM obtains F1 0.925, κSRME 0.170 and RMSD 0.0608 in Table 3, with additional phonon results in Table 4. These involve different training conditions, not same-setting gains over v1. For retained Table 2 entries, eSEN's κSRME changes from 0.321 to 0.340 and eqV2 S DeNS from 1.665 to 1.676, without a stated protocol change. Existing MDR rows, SPICE results and architecture-ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the conservative-force condition, energy-drift bound, differentiability assumptions and associated mathematical reasoning. No theorem, proof, derivation or formal definition is added or substantively revised in the main text or appendices.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the benchmark leadership claim to non-compliant Matbench-Discovery models, reporting F1 0.925 and κSRME 0.170. Section 6.2 similarly extends the phonon SOTA wording to both categories. The central contribution concerning energy conservation, smooth potentials and the usefulness of test errors remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 adds a substantive qualification that OMat-only phonon results should not be directly compared because the DFT settings differ. It also attributes their lower errors to avoiding softening associated with sAlex/MPTrj. The existing interpretations of conservation, displacement sensitivity and phonon failure modes remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit checkpoint-access link and expands Appendix D's hyperparameter table with OMat training and OAM fine-tuning settings, including the data mixture, budgets, basis count, batch sizes and learning rates. It also newly states that MDR covers around 10,000 materials; this is additional documentation, not evidence of a changed sample size. Existing implementation and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Deng et al. on systematic softening, Yin et al. on AlphaNet and Rhodes et al. on Orb-v3. Sections 5.1 and 7 additionally credit Bigi et al. for the direct-force pretraining/conservative fine-tuning strategy, refining its attribution without broadly changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: The revision makes local wording and terminology edits, distinguishes MP and OAM model names, and adds paragraphs about non-compliant results and DFT compatibility. The abstract's substance, section sequence, central narrative and appendix organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the non-compliant Matbench table, expands the compliant, phonon and hyperparameter tables, and changes their row/column organization and captions. Figure 6 moves relative to Section 6.4, with associated page reflow. The plotted content of the existing main-text and appendix figures is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence that eSEN remains useful beyond MPTrj-only training while separating the training regimes in its comparisons. The new training recipes, checkpoint-access information, attribution and DFT-mismatch qualification improve reproducibility and interpretation. However, the broader phonon SOTA wording needs qualification: Table 4 gives SevenNet-MF-ompa lower entropy and free-energy errors than eSEN-30M-OAM, 8 versus 10 and 3 versus 4. The net improvement is limited, with the core method and original validation unchanged.
